cards.explanation: The answer is the doors, friends. Nehemiah says, "When the wall had been rebuilt and I had set the doors in place…" (Nehemiah 7:1). A wall with a gap in it is just a very long suggestion. The doors are what finish the job.
The answer is gatekeepers. The verse says "…the gatekeepers, singers, and Levites were appointed." (Nehemiah 7:1). Doors need somebody standing by them, or they're just fancy wood.

The answer is that he was faithful and feared God more than most, friends. Nehemiah says he put Hananiah, the commander of the fortress, in charge "…because he was a faithful man who feared God more than most." (Nehemiah 7:2). Notice what he doesn't list: muscles, a big résumé or a fancy title. I'd have been picked for my mustache and been very wrong.

The answer is False. Nehemiah says, "Do not open the gates of Jerusalem until the sun is hot." (Nehemiah 7:3). He adds, "While the guards are on duty, keep the doors shut and securely fastened." So the gates wait for the heat of the day, not first light.

The answer is the residents of Jerusalem, friends, the people who live there. Nehemiah says, "…appoint the residents of Jerusalem as guards, some at their posts and some at their own homes." (Nehemiah 7:3). Imagine your neighbors on guard duty. I'd be the guy at my own house guarding the cookie jar.

The answer is few, bakers. The verse says, "Now the city was large and spacious, but there were few people in it…" (Nehemiah 7:4). That same verse adds that "…the houses had not yet been rebuilt." Lots of room, few people.

The answer is True, friends. The verse says "…the houses had not yet been rebuilt." (Nehemiah 7:4). The same verse says "Now the city was large and spacious, but there were few people in it…" So there's a finished wall and a lot of open room, but the homes aren't back yet.

The answer is genealogy, friends. The verse says God put it into Nehemiah's heart to gather the people "…to be enrolled by genealogy." (Nehemiah 7:5). That means family lines, who came from whom. Nehemiah says it was his God who put it in his heart.

The answer is the register of those who first returned, friends. Nehemiah says, "I found the genealogical register of those who had first returned…" (Nehemiah 7:5). He wanted people enrolled by family, and the list was already written down. Some folks get a lucky find, and some of us just get a stale takeout menu.

The answer is False, friends. The text says the priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, temple servants and the rest of the Israelites "…settled in their own towns." (Nehemiah 7:73). They didn't all move inside Jerusalem's walls.
